Adds deterministic control, but requires a Codex runtime driver that translates Codex's event stream into Barkpark's sink-tuple contract. Larger build; the driver is the risk.

Provider-neutral shared state passed between heterogeneous agents is exactly what the field's durable-orchestration systems do. Microsoft Magentic-One runs a dual Task Ledger + Progress Ledger as its coordination substrate (arXiv:2411.04468). Google's A2A protocol separates contextId (the conversation) from taskId (one stateful unit of work), with task lifecycle states submitted→working→completed/failed. Both map directly onto the bp claim/close/epoch ledger + the wave Paper — so Barkpark's spine is a recognized pattern, not an invention.

blocks.title: The ledger-as-spine bet is a named, proven architecture

items.value: The bp task ledger — claim/close with epoch-CAS, MCP-native. Claude reads it via native tools; Codex reads the SAME board through bp mcp serve (docs/setup/CODEX.md). One truth, two providers.

The capability matrix + readiness probe (api/lib/barkpark/studio_chat/capabilities.ex, probe.ex) already declare three lanes :claude | :bp | :codex, with codex/0 an explicit all-false stub — the router's brain, pre-wired for the provider axis.

The chat renderer already dispatches on tool-call SHAPE, not provider name (charter D40: the cmux fork emits Agent where vanilla emits Task; D39: TodoWrite absent on one binary). The rendering layer is already provider-agnostic.

blocks.text: Finding 1 — provider routing is a solved abstraction

content.value: Every multi-provider framework converges on a provider/model handle plus optional cost/latency/capability routing: LiteLLM Router (cost-based/latency-based strategies), OpenRouter (models[] fallback + provider.sort price|throughput|latency), Vercel AI SDK (createProviderRegistry, provider:model), LangChain init_chat_model('openai:gpt-5.5'), CrewAI Agent(llm=...), AutoGen per-agent model_client, Mastra provider/model. This validates the plan's core move: give agent() a provider dimension — agent(prompt, {provider:'codex', model:'gpt-5.x'}) — the industry-standard abstraction.

blocks.text: Finding 2 — the wire formats are incompatible, and MCP does NOT level them

content.value: Anthropic defines tools with input_schema and returns a tool_use block whose input is a parsed OBJECT; results come back as a tool_result block inside a USER message; tool args stream as input_json_delta/partial_json. OpenAI Chat Completions wraps tools under function{parameters}, returns tool_calls whose arguments is a JSON STRING, and feeds results as a role:'tool' message. OpenAI's own Responses API differs again (flat function, call_id vs tool_call_id). MCP does NOT fix this: it is a host↔server discovery/execution protocol (JSON-RPC: tools/list, tools/call) that both vendors bolt on ABOVE their unchanged native function-calling. The real levelers are SDK/gateway layers (Vercel AI SDK, LiteLLM translate-all-to-OpenAI). Consequence: Route A avoids this entirely (each provider native); Route B must own the translation in the driver.

blocks.title: Native tool-call formats diverge — even within OpenAI's own stack

blocks.text: Finding 3 — Codex ships clean headless surfaces (the driver shrinks)

content.value: Codex exposes three normalized headless surfaces: (1) codex exec --json — a JSON Lines event stream (thread.started, turn.started/completed/failed, item.*, error) with codex exec resume <SESSION_ID> and --output-schema for JSON-Schema-constrained output; (2) codex mcp-server — Codex runs AS an MCP server over JSON-RPC/stdio, exposing codex (start) + codex-reply (continue, carrying threadId); (3) an official TypeScript SDK @openai/codex-sdk wrapping codex exec --json. A driver therefore mirrors claude_chat.ex's NDJSON parse against Codex's documented event contract — not a raw wire translation. This drops the Codex driver from LARGE toward MEDIUM. Codex also configures MCP servers in ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.*], so bp mcp serve plugs in with zero new code (latest CLI 0.144.2, now a Rust binary; example model gpt-5.5).

blocks.title: Consume Codex's own event vocabulary, not raw OpenAI wire format

blocks.text: Finding 4 — provider-diverse verification is well-motivated (not head-to-head proven)

content.value: Two independent, peer-reviewed motivations: (1) LLM judges favor their OWN outputs — self-preference bias causally tied to self-recognition (Panickssery et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2404.13076; Wataoka et al., arXiv:2410.21819). (2) Intrinsic same-model self-correction is unreliable and can DEGRADE reasoning without external feedback (Huang et al., ICLR 2024, arXiv:2310.01798). Diverse-model ensembles raise quality: Mixture-of-Agents beat GPT-4 Omni 65.1 vs 57.5 on AlpacaEval 2.0 (Wang et al., ICLR 2025, arXiv:2406.04692). Production practice codifies judge ≠ generator (DeepEval; adversarial-judge pipelines). HONEST CAVEAT: no fetched paper A/B-tests same-model vs different-model critique as its headline result — the support is strong but indirect. Defensible claim: well-motivated, not proven superior head-to-head.

blocks.title: The peer-reviewed case for a different-provider judge

content.value: The provider AXIS is SMALL–MEDIUM: thread a provider atom through Recorder.ensure → session_opts (recorder.ex ~L110-123), add a provider column to chat_sessions (new migration; none exists today), introduce a provider→driver module map, and point the Studio pickers at Capabilities.<provider>() instead of ClaudeChat.* directly (chat_live.ex ~L2836/2855/2883, and the parallel /v1/chat SSE transport in chat_controller.ex). The sink-tuple vocabulary ({:claude_chat_event|exit|permission|control}) is already a provider-neutral boundary, and the renderer is already shape-dispatched.

The working Codex DRIVER is MEDIUM (down from LARGE thanks to Finding 3): mirror claude_chat.ex against codex exec --json. The five contract points now have concrete answers — session identity/resume = thread_id + codex exec resume; permission round-trip = approval_policy (untrusted/on-request/never) + mcp_elicitations; headless = codex exec; structured output = --output-schema; result metrics = the turn.completed event. The Workflow harness (bp-epic-cycle) is a Claude Code harness feature outside api/, model: enums locked to Anthropic aliases — out of scope for this repo.

items.value: P0 — Route A weave (now): point a Codex CLI and a Claude CLI at the same bp board via bp mcp serve; drive a real cross-provider task claim→close through the ledger. Gate: one task claimed by Claude and one by Codex, both closed with evidence on the same board.

P1 — Provider axis (contract only): add the provider dimension + driver seam; Codex stays an honest enabled?:false stub. Gate: a session spawns with provider=:claude unchanged, and pickers/probe read the selected provider's capabilities.

P2 — Codex driver spike → build: prove codex exec --json satisfies the five contract points, then build codex_chat.ex emitting the same sink tuples. Gate: a Codex-backed Studio chat session completes a real task claim→close through the driver.

P3 — Routing policy + surface: route by capability-fit / cost / latency / explicit pin; add a provider selector to Studio chat and (optionally) provider-diverse verification. Gate: a workflow runs one Fable step and one Codex step and returns both.
Wire-format translation (Route B) — mitigated by consuming Codex's --json event contract, not raw OpenAI wire, and by keeping the sink-tuple boundary + shape-dispatch renderer that already exist.
Capability divergence hidden by stubs — P2 gates routing on a real probe before policy trusts it; capabilities.codex/0 is already explicit-false by design.
Auth & secrets across two providers — reuse the env_vars secret-forwarding contract (bp and Codex) and Codex's OPENAI_API_KEY / ChatGPT sign-in; never interpolate tokens into config.
Cost & determinism — explicit per-step pinning stays available; provider-diversity is opt-in per workflow.
A real Claude⇄Codex weave runs through the bp ledger (Route A).
The provider axis spawns a claude session unchanged and reads per-provider capabilities.
A Codex-backed session completes a task claim→close via the driver.
One opt-in provider-diverse verification pass with an auditable ledger trail.

Feasibility (grounded in the code)

The provider AXIS is SMALL–MEDIUM: thread a provider atom through Recorder.ensure → session_opts (recorder.ex ~L110-123), add a provider column to chat_sessions (new migration; none exists today), introduce a provider→driver module map, and point the Studio pickers at Capabilities.<provider>() instead of ClaudeChat.* directly (chat_live.ex ~L2836/2855/2883, and the parallel /v1/chat SSE transport in chat_controller.ex). The sink-tuple vocabulary ({:claude_chat_event|exit|permission|control}) is already a provider-neutral boundary, and the renderer is already shape-dispatched.

The working Codex DRIVER is MEDIUM (down from LARGE thanks to Finding 3): mirror claude_chat.ex against codex exec --json. The five contract points now have concrete answers — session identity/resume = thread_id + codex exec resume; permission round-trip = approval_policy (untrusted/on-request/never) + mcp_elicitations; headless = codex exec; structured output = --output-schema; result metrics = the turn.completed event. The Workflow harness (bp-epic-cycle) is a Claude Code harness feature outside api/, model: enums locked to Anthropic aliases — out of scope for this repo.

Recommended phased plan

• P0 — Route A weave (now): point a Codex CLI and a Claude CLI at the same bp board via bp mcp serve; drive a real cross-provider task claim→close through the ledger. Gate: one task claimed by Claude and one by Codex, both closed with evidence on the same board.
• P1 — Provider axis (contract only): add the provider dimension + driver seam; Codex stays an honest enabled?:false stub. Gate: a session spawns with provider=:claude unchanged, and pickers/probe read the selected provider's capabilities.
• P2 — Codex driver spike → build: prove codex exec --json satisfies the five contract points, then build codex_chat.ex emitting the same sink tuples. Gate: a Codex-backed Studio chat session completes a real task claim→close through the driver.
• P3 — Routing policy + surface: route by capability-fit / cost / latency / explicit pin; add a provider selector to Studio chat and (optionally) provider-diverse verification. Gate: a workflow runs one Fable step and one Codex step and returns both.

Risks & mitigations

• Wire-format translation (Route B) — mitigated by consuming Codex's --json event contract, not raw OpenAI wire, and by keeping the sink-tuple boundary + shape-dispatch renderer that already exist.
• Capability divergence hidden by stubs — P2 gates routing on a real probe before policy trusts it; capabilities.codex/0 is already explicit-false by design.
• Auth & secrets across two providers — reuse the env_vars secret-forwarding contract (bp and Codex) and Codex's OPENAI_API_KEY / ChatGPT sign-in; never interpolate tokens into config.
• Cost & determinism — explicit per-step pinning stays available; provider-diversity is opt-in per workflow.

Success criteria

• A real Claude⇄Codex weave runs through the bp ledger (Route A).
• The provider axis spawns a claude session unchanged and reads per-provider capabilities.
• A Codex-backed session completes a task claim→close via the driver.
• One opt-in provider-diverse verification pass with an auditable ledger trail.

Sources

Orchestration & routing: LiteLLM docs; OpenRouter routing/provider-selection docs; Vercel AI SDK provider-management + AI Gateway; LangChain init_chat_model reference; CrewAI agents docs; AutoGen model-client docs; Mastra model-router blog. Hand-off & ledgers: OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs; OpenAI Swarm; A2A spec (a2a-protocol.org); Magentic-One (arXiv:2411.04468); LangGraph persistence docs.

Tool-call formats: platform.claude.com tool-use + streaming; developers.openai.com function-calling; modelcontextprotocol.io. Verification: arXiv:2404.13076, 2410.21819, 2310.01798, 2305.14325, 2406.04692; DeepEval. Codex CLI: learn.chatgpt.com/docs (config-reference, mcp, non-interactive-mode, codex-sdk, sandboxing, auth); openai/codex codex_mcp_interface.md + releases (0.144.2, 2026-07-13).

Open questions for a reviewer
(a) Surface-first: should the first conductor weave target the Workflow harness (batch) or Studio chat (interactive)? This plan does Route A first regardless. (b) Coupling: every step through the ledger, or only checkpoint boundaries? (c) Is provider-diverse verification worth shipping given the honest caveat, or should the first demo be cheaper capability-routing?
